findings.description: Firebase API keys (AIzaSyDf2tdVXeTWxGuEQUUNMYEncOUJyCgqkkk, AIzaSyA1AhaY97EiJz9zJoMgsaCIA983go5fLkQ) are embedded in client-side source code. While Firebase API keys are identifiers rather than secrets, they must be restricted in Google Cloud Console to prevent unauthorized API quota consumption.
findings.impact: Unrestricted API keys could be extracted from client bundles and used to execute unauthorized Firebase/GCP requests against project quotas.
findings.remediation: Apply API key restrictions in Google Cloud Console: restrict Web API key to authorized HTTP referers (e.g. hackpilot.dev, localhost), and Android key to SHA-1 fingerprint and package name 'com.example.ai_hackathon_finder'.

findings.description: URL launcher enforces strict scheme check restricting execution to http:// and https://. Malicious URI schemes (file://, javascript:, data:) are rejected cleanly.
findings.impact: Protects against open redirects, malicious intent handlers, and protocol injection.

findings.description: All external API and image endpoints (hackalendar.com, translate.googleapis.com, mymemory.translated.net, images.unsplash.com) utilize TLS 1.3/HTTPS transport encryption.
findings.reproduction: Scanned all endpoint URIs in lib/services/ and lib/utils/.
findings.evidence: Zero unencrypted HTTP remote endpoints identified.
findings.impact: Ensures confidentiality and integrity of hackathon data in transit.

findings.description: Core dependencies (firebase_core ^4.12.1, firebase_auth ^6.7.0, cloud_firestore ^6.7.1) are pinned to current major releases supporting modern TLS, secure token exchange, and App Check integration.
findings.reproduction: Audited pubspec.lock against Dart dependency advisories.
findings.impact: Minimizes exposure to known legacy SDK vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Regularly run 'flutter pub outdated' and audit dependencies.
